ad: TAŞKIN v. TÜRKİYE and 10 other applications
paragraflar: Published on 28 September 2026
Application no. 43792/21 Hasan TAŞKIN against Türkiye and 10 other applications (see list appended) communicated on 7 September 2026
SUBJECT MATTER OF THE CASE

The applications concern disciplinary sanctions imposed on the applicants (for details regarding the nature of and reasons given for the sanctions, see the Appendix), civil servants at the material time, on account of their participation in certain public assemblies, such as marches and demonstrations, and/or making press statements and chanting slogans during these assemblies.

The domestic authorities considered that the disciplinary sanctions for the impugned participation in assemblies and statements were appropriate and necessary given the duties incumbent upon the applicants by virtue of their civil servant status.
Invoking Articles 10 and 11 of the Convention, the applicants complain that the disciplinary sanctions in question breached their rights to freedom of expression and freedom of peaceful assembly.

In addition, invoking Article 6 § 1 of the Convention, the applicants in application no. 49730/21 complained about the length of the proceedings before the Constitutional Court. The proceedings concerned lasted between approximately three years and six months and three years and ten months respectively.

1. Has there been an interference with the applicants’ right to freedom of expression and/or freedom of peaceful assembly, within the meaning of Articles 10 § 1 and 11 § 1 of the Convention, on account of the sanctions imposed upon them (see Vogt v. Germany, 26 September 1995, §§ 44 and 65, Series A no. 323, and Kula v. Turkey, no. 20233/06, §§ 36-40, 19 June 2018)?

2. If so, was that interference prescribed by law and necessary in a democratic society within the meaning of Articles 10 § 2 and/or 11 § 2 (see, for the general principles, Baka v. Hungary [GC], no. 20261/12, §§ 158-62, 23 June 2016; Ezelin v. France, 26 April 1991, §§ 42-53, Series A no. 202, and Dedecan and Ok v. Turkey, nos. 22685/09; and 39472/09, §§ 30-41, 22 September 2015)?

3. Having regard to the circumstances of each case, in particular, the applicants’ participation in the impugned public assemblies, the content of the statements made during these assemblies, and the context in which they were expressed, did the national courts carry out a sufficient examination and strike a proper balance between the interests at stake, in the light of the criteria set out by the Court in its case-law on freedom of expression and freedom of peaceful assembly (see Baka, cited above, § 162; Ezelin, cited above, §§ 51-53; Öğrü and Others v. Turkey, nos. 60087/10 and 2 others, §§ 66-70, 19 December 2017; and Kula v. Turkey, cited above, §§ 44-52)?
Additional question for application no. 49730/21

4. Were the proceedings before the Constitutional Court in application no. 49730/21 concluded within a “reasonable time” in accordance with Article 6 § 1 of the Convention (see Frydlender v. France [GC], no. 30979/96, § 43, ECHR 2000-VII; Ümmühan Kaplan v. Turkey, no. 24240/07, § 45, 20 March 2012, and Project-Trade d.o.o. v. Croatia, no. 1920/14, §§ 99-104, 19 November 2020)?
